plain: A coming or stepping in between; intervention.

webster.text: A being, placing or coming between; intervention; as the interposition of the Baltic sea between Germany and Sweden.

more.text: Intervenient agency; as the interposition of the magistrate in quieting sedition.

example.quote: All conspiracies and plots against the government, which have not been matured into actual treason, may be screened from punishment of every kind, by the interposition of the prerogative of pardoning.
